title: Prentice Gautt: OU Pioneer Who Became a Conference Executive
question: What did Prentice Gautt, OU's first Black football player, do after football?
answer: Prentice Gautt, OU's first Black football player (1956-59), earned a Ph.D. in counseling psychology and became an associate commissioner of the Big Eight and later the Big 12.
summary: Prentice Gautt, OU's first Black football player (1956-59), earned a Ph.D. in counseling psychology and became a Big Eight and Big 12 associate commissioner.
body: Prentice Gautt was an All-State running back at Oklahoma City's Douglass High School when he joined the Sooners in the fall of 1956, becoming the first Black football player at OU. Black doctors and pharmacists in Oklahoma City funded his scholarship at first, and within two months Bud Wilkinson put him on an athletic scholarship.

Gautt played from 1956 to 1959 and became a starter in 1958. In the Orange Bowl played in January 1959, he averaged a record 15.7 yards per carry, including a 42-yard touchdown run, and was named the game's MVP. He earned All-Big Eight honors twice and was an Academic All-American as a senior.

After a pro career that began with the Cleveland Browns, Gautt moved into coaching and academics. He joined the University of Missouri as an assistant coach, then shifted to academic counseling for athletes, and in 1975 he earned a doctorate in counseling psychology from Missouri.

His biggest impact came in conference leadership. Gautt joined the Big Eight staff in 1979, became associate commissioner in 1983 and senior associate commissioner in 1994. When the Big 12 formed, he became an associate commissioner there and later a special assistant to the commissioner. He also served as secretary-treasurer of the NCAA.

OU named its athletics academic center for him in 1999, a fitting honor for a man who opened doors on the field and then spent decades helping athletes succeed in the classroom. Gautt died in March 2005.
